text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the lung arteries, making it hard for the heart to pump blood.
snippet_highlighted_words: high blood pressure in the lung arteries

list.snippet: Shortness of breath (dyspnea): Often starts during physical activity (like climbing stairs or exercising) and eventually happens even at rest.
Fatigue and weakness: Feeling unusually tired because the body lacks sufficient oxygen flow.
Chest pain or pressure: Caused by the extra strain placed on the right side of the heart.
Dizziness or fainting (syncope): Results from reduced blood flow and lower blood pressure to the brain.
Edema (swelling): Fluid buildup in the ankles, feet, legs, and eventually the abdomen or neck.
Heart palpitations: A fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat.
Cyanosis: A bluish or grayish tint to the lips, skin, or fingers due to low oxygen.
Other signs: A dry cough, hoarseness, or lack of appetite as the condition progresses.

text_blocks.snippet: More detailed information on tracking and recognizing these signs can be found through the American Lung Association and the Cleveland Clinic.
If you or someone you know is experiencing these signs, sharing when the symptoms started or whether they happen at rest or during activity can help me provide more relevant details.
